concepts.title: Voice Dialogue: The Method of Moving Chairs
concepts.excerpt: Here is the simplest version of what Voice Dialogue does: instead of talking about your inner critic, you move to a different chair and talk as it.

concepts.title: Primary and Disowned Selves: The Committee and Its Exiles
concepts.excerpt: You are, right now, living primarily from two or three internal voices.

concepts.title: The Aware Ego: The Witness That Holds the Contradictions
concepts.excerpt: Most people, most of the time, are not driving the car. One of their internal voices is driving.

concepts.title: The Protector/Controller: The Original Guardian
concepts.excerpt: Every person has a self whose job is to make sure nothing dangerous gets through.

concepts.title: The Heavyweights: The Infrastructure of the Defended Self
concepts.excerpt: Imagine the ego as a factory floor. The Heavyweights are the shift supervisors — the voices that have been running production longest, hardest, and with the least tolerance for downtime.

concepts.title: The Power-Vulnerability Paradox: Why Strength Needs What It Suppresses
concepts.excerpt: A well-dressed man from a small country drives a huge Rolls Royce through America.

concepts.title: Archetypal Bonding Patterns: The Dance That Runs on Its Own
concepts.excerpt: When the good mother and the needy child meet — regardless of who is the parent and who is the child, regardless of whether the interaction is between generations or between lovers or between colleagues — something clicks into place that is larger than either person.

concepts.title: Demonic Transformation Through Honor: The Caged Animal and the Open Door
concepts.excerpt: Here is the idea that upends most of what we think we know about psychological darkness: the demonic is not something you were born with.

concepts.title: Spirituality vs. Consciousness: The Map That Mistakes Itself for the Territory
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a ladder with forty rungs. A person grabs the third rung, pulls themselves up, looks down at the ground, feels the altitude, and decides they have reached the top.

concepts.title: Voice Dialogue Framework: Direct Conversation with Your Inner Multitudes
concepts.excerpt: You are not one unified self speaking with one voice.

concepts.title: Operating Ego vs. Aware Ego: The Difference Between Running Your Life and Observing It
concepts.excerpt: At any moment, your consciousness exists in one of two modes. In the Operating Ego mode, you are identified with whatever primary self is active.

concepts.title: Inner Critic (Core): The Protective Voice That Became a Tyrant
concepts.excerpt: Imagine you're driving down the highway and the radio has been on so long you've stopped hearing it.

concepts.title: Subpersonality Pairs: Primary Self and Its Banished Opposite
concepts.excerpt: Inside you exists a hidden law: every primary self you developed has an equal and opposite self that you banished.

concepts.title: The Incomparable Comparer: The Mechanism That Maintains Shame Through Endless Measuring
concepts.excerpt: You walk into a room. Your Incomparable Comparer is already awake. Within seconds, it has scanned everyone there and created a hierarchy.

concepts.title: "What Will People Think?": The Relational Anxiety That Shapes Identity
concepts.excerpt: At the root of much Inner Critic activity lives a specific anxiety: What will people think?

concepts.title: The Rule Maker: The Legislator of Your Inner World
concepts.excerpt: Inside many people lives a particular subpersonality: the Rule Maker. This is not the same as the Perfectionist, though they often work together.

concepts.title: Disowned Self Projection and Judgment: Mirror Mechanism for Self-Discovery
concepts.excerpt: Here's a reliable psychological mirror: the things you judge most harshly in other people are often the things you've disowned in yourself.

concepts.title: Personal vs. Impersonal Energy: The Quality of Your Presence
concepts.excerpt: The Stones identify a distinction that applies across all human interaction and expression: the difference between personal energy and impersonal energy.

concepts.title: Bonding Patterns: How the Critic Creates Specific Relational Dynamics
concepts.excerpt: The Stones identify a specific relational dynamic that emerges when the Inner Critic becomes dominant: what they call "bonding patterns."

concepts.title: Inner Child Abuse Cycle: The System That Perpetuates Shame
concepts.excerpt: Here is something the Stones teach that can be shocking when you first encounter it: the Inner Critic, which originated as a protective voice, eventually becomes an abuser.

concepts.title: Shame, Depression, and Low Self-Esteem Cycle: The Interlocking System
concepts.excerpt: Understanding the distinction between these three is important, though, because they have slightly different entry points and slightly different characteristics.

concepts.title: IFS: The Mono-Mind Paradigm
concepts.excerpt: Everyone in the Western world walks around running an operating system they never chose.

concepts.title: IFS: Parts as Innate
concepts.excerpt: Here is the claim that IFS makes and that most psychology quietly refuses: the multiplicity of your mind is not the wound.

concepts.title: IFS Parts Taxonomy
concepts.excerpt: Your mind is not one person. It is a household — and like any household under sustained pressure, it develops a structure.

concepts.title: IFS Self and Self-Leadership
concepts.excerpt: There is a difference between managing yourself and being managed by your parts.

concepts.title: IFS: Fractal and Nested Self
concepts.excerpt: The standard model of the psyche is an onion: peel away enough defensive layers and you arrive at a single core self at the center.

concepts.title: IFS Inner Work Methods
concepts.excerpt: Before any of the three access methods can begin, there must be an entry point into the internal system.

concepts.title: IFS Burden and Unburdening
concepts.excerpt: Imagine carrying a backpack so long you've forgotten it's not part of your body.

concepts.title: IFS: Laws of Inner Physics
concepts.excerpt: Most of what happens in an internal system — the particular parts a person has, the specific burdens they carry, the exact configuration of their Manager-Firefighter-Exile ecology — is completely individual.

concepts.title: The Objective Mind: The Critic Transformed Into Creative Ally
concepts.excerpt: The Stones teach that the endpoint of the Inner Critic work is not the destruction or silencing of the Critic.

concepts.title: Journal Writing and Voice Dialogue as Method: Practice That Allows Separation
concepts.excerpt: The Stones teach that Voice Dialogue, while most powerful when facilitated by a trained practitioner, can be practiced individually through written dialogue.

concepts.title: IFS: Spiritual and Somatic Dimensions
concepts.excerpt: Most psychological frameworks treat the body as a container for the mind's contents, and the spirit as something outside both — either irrelevant to clinical work or available only to those who have adopted a specific religious or metaphysical commitment.

concepts.title: IFS: Relational and Collective Applications
concepts.excerpt: Internal Family Systems began as individual therapy. One person, one practitioner, one internal system to explore.

concepts.title: IFS Cultural and Societal Application
concepts.excerpt: Most psychotherapy has a hidden assumption: the goal is to help you function better in your culture.

concepts.title: Bipolar Shadow Architecture: Consciousness Dissociation in Two Forms
concepts.excerpt: Freudian and Jungian psychology typically describe the shadow as what consciousness represses — the unacceptable aspects of self that are pushed into the unconscious and hidden.

concepts.title: Dissociation and Attacks on Linking: The BASK Model
concepts.excerpt: Imagine someone describing the worst thing that ever happened to them in a voice completely flat, as though reading a grocery list.

concepts.title: The Protector-Persecutor Dyad: Dual Faces of a Single Protective Structure
concepts.excerpt: While the Protector and Persecutor may be experienced as separate entities, they are actually dual manifestations of a single archetypal protective system.

concepts.title: Arousal and Emotional Response: The Body's Persisting Alarm
concepts.excerpt: Suppression removes cognitive content from consciousness. A person suppresses a thought about harm and the thought is no longer consciously present.

concepts.title: Energy Dancer: Working with Energy States as a Living Practice
concepts.excerpt: The Stones teach that the endpoint of their work is not the development of a perfect psyche with all parts integrated into harmony.

concepts.title: Shadow Integration
concepts.excerpt: Every personality has a sealed room.
